title: safety-review-scratchpad-for-small-batch-reverts-isaac
content:
Purpose:
This is a messy personal scratchpad for handling small-batch PR rollouts that look risky and might need fast reversion. Not a formal playbook yet — distills my day-to-day checklist, quick heuristics, and communication snippets to use during a hot revert.

Context & recent signal patterns:
- Root cause types I care about: latency regressions, memory OOMs on 1-2 hosts, egregious cost spikes, data-path contract breakage (schema/marshalling), and quiet feature flags that flip behavior server-side.
- Recent example: PR #4821 introduced incremental KV-cache change. Autotest passed; slow rollout -> 3% p50 latency jump on a single AZ; errors spiked ~0.4% on route /chat/stream.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 min):
- Confirm the deployment id + exact git sha. 
- Check deploy timeline (who kicked, canary percentage, autoscale events).
- Pinpoint signal: latency / errors / resource / logs. Grab top-5 traces in Sentry/Tracing.
- Rollback switch? Does the deployment support immediate rollback via console or need manual job?
- Communicate: post to #prod-incidents with short TL;DR + rollback intent.

Decision rubric: do we revert? (fast heuristics)
- Yes if: user-visible errors >0.1% absolute or p99 latency increase >200ms for >5min or memory OOMs on >1 host.
- Consider partial hold (pause rollout) if: localized spike in one region, nondeterministic failure rate <0.05% and no data corruption risk.
- No if: metric blip <1min, attributable to infra fluke (node reboot), or fix can be hotpatched with confidence <20min and low risk.

Rollback execution steps:
1) Pause rollout in console (if canary) OR kick directed rollback job.
2) If console unresponsive: run CLI rollback: 
   - git checkout <previous-sha> && deploy --target <cluster> --force --reason "rollback: revert PR #4821"
   - kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> -n prod --to-revision=<rev> (double-check rollout history)
3) Watch health checks & consumer metrics (p50, p95, errors) for next 10m.
4) If rollback fails or pods crash: escalate to SRE (tag: oncall) and run emergency scaling (increase replicas to absorb traffic).

Communication templates (Slack snippet):
- Initial: "Observing elevated errors and latency on /chat/stream after canary. Pausing rollout and starting rollback to prior sha. PR: #4821. Owner: @isaac. Will post updates."
- Post-rollback: "Rollback complete to sha abc123. p95 latency and error-rate back to baseline within 6m. Investigating root cause. Follow-up doc incoming."

Post-revert follow-ups / TO-DOs:
- Collect traces: save 10 slow traces pre-rollback and 10 post-rollback for diffing.
- Reproduce locally with same traffic shape (prefab script: tools/loadtest/kv-cache-load.sh).
- Add stricter canary evaluation: add p99 and 5xx thresholds to automated canary gate.
- Add regression test: synthetic trace-run to catch worst-case path (long sequence, cache fill).
- Owner retro: request a brief doc from PR author explaining assumptions + load-profile used.

Hypotheses to test:
- Cache change increases CPU per token due to extra copy -> target kernel hotpath. CPU sample + flamegraph.
- Background eviction causing KV thrash -> increase mem pressure -> GC pause. Check heap profiles.

Ops snippets (notes):
- Useful commands: 
   - gh pr view 4821 --json commits,files 
   - kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=chat -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount}'
   - curl -sS "https://tracing/redwood/api?service=chat&span=slow" | jq 'map(.duration) | add / length'

Unresolved questions (notes-to-self):
- Can we make canary gate evaluate memory deltas, not just error/latency? Need metric team input.
- Should rollbacks be automated for OOMs? Danger: noisy OOMs could flip back-and-forth. Maybe add debounce.
- Who owns the rollback runbook doc? Suggest SRE + serving-runtime co-own.

Short-term TODOs (today):
- Share this scratchpad with Harper + Mina, get buy-in on the decision rubric.
- Prototype canary gate that watches p99 + heap delta by EOD.
- Save traces from previous incident and tag as "kv-cache-2025-01".

Misc scratch notes (brain dump):
- Keep revert messages terse but include PR and reason. Avoid blame.
- Consider a "soft revert" that disables new feature flag instead of full code revert when feasible.
- Metric to add: % of deploys that triggered rollbacks in past 90 days (for trend).

End of scratchpad. This is messy — intended for quick copy/paste and iteration.
